questions.stem: Mrs Bello plans how to use the family's money, time and energy so that the children's school needs are met. This activity is best described as
questions.explanation: Home management is planning and using family resources to reach family goals.

questions.stem: Which of these careers is related to home management?
questions.explanation: Interior decoration, catering, dietetics, fashion design and laundry services all draw on home management.

questions.stem: Mr Adeyemi writes down what must be done for his daughter's wedding, by whom and by what date. This stage of management is
questions.explanation: Deciding in advance what to do, how, by whom and when is planning, the first stage of management.

questions.stem: Checking whether a plan was successful after it has been carried out is called
questions.explanation: Evaluation compares results with the goals set.

questions.stem: Ideas or beliefs which a family considers important and worthwhile are its
questions.explanation: Values are deep beliefs about what is desirable; goals are ends to be achieved.

questions.stem: A family that sets out to build its own house within five years has set a
questions.explanation: Goals that take years to achieve are long-term goals.

questions.stem: A mother who insists that the floor must be swept exactly as her own mother did it, whatever the circumstance, is showing a
questions.explanation: Conventional standards are fixed, traditional measures of quality; flexible standards adapt to circumstances.

questions.stem: Which pair consists only of human resources?
questions.explanation: Human resources are within people: time, energy, skills, knowledge, abilities, attitudes.

questions.stem: A town hall, a public library and a primary health centre available to every family in Ilesa are
questions.explanation: Facilities provided for everyone in the community are community resources.

questions.stem: Which characteristic is common to ALL family resources?
options: They are available only to adults
questions.explanation: All resources are limited; they can often be substituted and must be used wisely.

questions.stem: Ngozi cannot decide how to spend her holiday. Before listing her options, she should
questions.explanation: Decision-making starts by identifying and defining the problem.

questions.stem: Decisions taken automatically without much thought, such as brushing the teeth each morning, are
questions.explanation: Habitual (routine) decisions are made almost automatically.

questions.stem: A family decides to relocate to Abuja; this then requires decisions on a new school, house and transport. The decision to relocate is a
questions.explanation: A central decision is a major one around which related (satellite) decisions are made.

questions.stem: Doing two tasks at the same time, such as boiling yam while washing plates, is called
questions.explanation: Dovetailing fits tasks together to save time.

questions.stem: The period of the day when the homemaker has the most work to do is known as the
questions.explanation: Peak load periods, such as mornings before school, need careful planning.

questions.stem: In kitchen planning, the work triangle connects the
options: dining table, door and window frame
questions.explanation: The work triangle links the three main work centres to reduce walking and save energy.

questions.stem: Tiredness caused by boredom, worry or lack of interest in a task is
questions.explanation: Psychological fatigue arises from mental states rather than physical effort.

questions.stem: Kemi lives with only her father, her mother and her two brothers. Her family type is
questions.explanation: The nuclear family consists of parents and their children.

questions.stem: A family formed when a widow with children marries a man who also has children is a
questions.explanation: A blended (step) family combines children from previous unions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of the family?
questions.explanation: Families reproduce, socialise, protect and provide for members.

questions.stem: Before Tunde and Amaka married, they spent two years studying each other's character and interests. This period is
questions.explanation: Courtship allows a couple to know each other before marriage.

questions.stem: A marriage conducted at a registry under the Marriage Act is a
questions.explanation: Statutory (court/registry) marriage is monogamous and governed by the Marriage Act.

questions.stem: A marriage in which a woman has more than one husband at the same time is
questions.explanation: Polyandry: one wife, several husbands; polygyny: one husband, several wives.

questions.stem: Regular medical check-ups given to a woman during pregnancy are called
questions.explanation: Antenatal care monitors mother and baby before birth.

questions.stem: Allowing an interval of two or more years between births mainly helps to
options: make the family grow as fast as possible
protect the health of mother and child
questions.explanation: Child spacing lets the mother recover and gives each child adequate care.

questions.stem: A meal that contains all the nutrients in the right proportions is a
questions.explanation: A balanced diet supplies every nutrient in correct amounts.

questions.stem: When planning family meals, the homemaker should FIRST consider the
questions.explanation: Meeting the nutritional needs of each member comes first, then cost, time and preferences.

questions.stem: Wearing uniforms by nurses and soldiers shows that clothing is used for
questions.explanation: Uniforms identify a person's occupation or group.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an item of household linen?
questions.explanation: Household linen includes bed linen, table linen and towels.

questions.stem: Which fibre is obtained from the cocoon of an insect?
questions.explanation: Silk is a protein fibre from the silkworm cocoon.

questions.stem: Which fibre is most likely to melt and form a hard bead when burnt?
questions.explanation: Thermoplastic synthetic fibres such as nylon melt and form hard beads.

questions.stem: The firmly woven edge running down both sides of a length of woven fabric is the
questions.explanation: The selvedge prevents the fabric from fraying along its length.

questions.stem: Fabric made by interlooping yarns is
questions.explanation: Knitting forms fabric by interlocking loops.

questions.stem: Taking stock of all the clothes one has before buying new ones is called a
questions.explanation: A wardrobe inventory shows what is available and what is needed.

questions.stem: In laundry, the first process before washing clothes is
questions.explanation: Clothes are sorted by colour, fabric and degree of soiling first.

questions.stem: Which treatment should be avoided on a fresh egg or blood stain because it sets the stain?
questions.explanation: Heat coagulates protein and fixes the stain; cold water loosens it.

questions.stem: Pinking shears are used mainly to
options: neaten raw edges to prevent fraying
cut neat buttonholes in thick fabrics
questions.explanation: Pinking shears cut a zigzag edge that limits fraying.

questions.stem: A tracing wheel is used together with
questions.explanation: The wheel transfers pattern markings to fabric through carbon paper.

questions.stem: A seam that encloses the raw edges completely and is suitable for thin, transparent fabrics is the
questions.explanation: The French seam is stitched twice so that raw edges are enclosed.

questions.stem: Mothballs (naphthalene) are placed among stored woollen garments in order to
questions.explanation: Naphthalene repels clothes moths whose larvae eat wool.

questions.stem: A house built with two or more floors, one above the other, is a
questions.explanation: A storey building (e.g. a duplex) has more than one floor.

questions.stem: Two houses built side by side sharing one common wall are
questions.explanation: Semi-detached houses are a pair joined by one party wall.

questions.stem: The most important factor when a low-income family chooses a house to rent is
options: its cost in relation to income
questions.explanation: Rent must be affordable within the family budget.

questions.stem: A family choosing a house should check the neighbourhood mainly for
options: the colour of the neighbouring roofs and fences
questions.explanation: Security, schools, markets, hospitals and transport are key location factors.

questions.stem: When setting up a new home with limited money, a couple should first buy
questions.explanation: Basic necessities come before luxuries.

questions.stem: A colour scheme using different tints and shades of only one colour is
questions.explanation: Monochromatic schemes use one hue in varying values.

questions.stem: A colour scheme made from colours next to each other on the colour wheel, such as yellow, yellow-green and green, is
questions.explanation: Analogous colours are neighbours on the wheel.

questions.stem: Light, cool colours are recommended for the walls of a small room mainly because they
questions.explanation: Light cool colours seem to recede, making small rooms look larger.

questions.stem: The unit used in charging consumers for electricity is the
questions.explanation: Electricity bills are based on energy used, measured in kilowatt-hours (units).

questions.stem: A 1000 W electric iron is used for 3 hours a day for 30 days. If one unit costs N200, the cost of using the iron is
questions.explanation: Energy = 1 kW x 3 h x 30 = 90 kWh; 90 x N200 = N18,000.

questions.stem: A device that cuts off electricity when too much current flows in a circuit is a
questions.explanation: Fuses and circuit breakers protect circuits from overload.

questions.stem: A dripping tap is usually repaired by
questions.explanation: A worn washer is the usual cause of a dripping tap.

questions.stem: A blocked kitchen sink can first be cleared by using a
questions.explanation: A rubber plunger forces the blockage out by pressure.

questions.stem: To prevent accidental poisoning of children in the home, medicines should be
questions.explanation: Medicines and chemicals must be stored safely out of children's reach.

questions.stem: The safest action when a pan of oil catches fire on the cooker is to
options: pour cold water into the burning pan quickly
switch off the heat and cover the pan
questions.explanation: Covering cuts off oxygen; water on burning oil spreads the fire.

questions.stem: Proper disposal of refuse in the home helps to prevent the
options: proper growth of potted house plants
questions.explanation: Uncovered refuse attracts flies, rats and other disease vectors.

questions.stem: Stagnant water in gutters around the house should be cleared mainly to prevent the breeding of
questions.explanation: Mosquitoes breed in stagnant water and spread malaria.

questions.stem: A person who starts and manages a business while bearing its risks is
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs initiate, organise and take the risks of business.

questions.stem: Turning used fabric pieces into attractive cushion covers for sale is an example of
questions.explanation: Creativity produces new useful products from ideas and materials.

questions.stem: A plan showing expected income and how it will be spent over a period is a
questions.explanation: A budget is a spending and saving plan.

questions.stem: A family spends 40% of its monthly income of N150,000 on food. The amount spent on food is
The satisfaction a person derives from goods and services, such as pleasure from a family outing, is
questions.explanation: Psychic income is the satisfaction derived from using resources.

questions.stem: The goods and services that money income can actually buy are called
questions.explanation: Real income measures purchasing power.

questions.stem: Which of these is a sound way for a family to create wealth?
questions.explanation: Regular saving and wise investment build wealth over time.

questions.stem: A part-owner of a public company who holds its shares is a
questions.explanation: Shareholders own part of the company.

questions.stem: The part of a company's profit paid out to shareholders is called a
questions.explanation: Dividends are profits distributed to shareholders.

questions.stem: Mrs Eze wants to report a firm that sold her fake shares. The government agency that regulates the capital market and to which she should report is the
questions.explanation: The SEC regulates and supervises the Nigerian capital market.

questions.stem: A licensed person who buys and sells shares on behalf of investors is a
questions.explanation: Stockbrokers deal in securities for clients on the exchange.

questions.topic: Definition and Importance of Consumer Education
questions.stem: Consumer education mainly helps people to
options: produce more goods in large factories
questions.explanation: It equips consumers to buy wisely and protect their interests.

questions.topic: Rights and Responsibilities of a Consumer
questions.stem: A consumer who complains when sold a faulty blender is exercising the right to
questions.explanation: The right to redress means compensation for unsatisfactory goods.

questions.topic: Rights and Responsibilities of a Consumer
questions.stem: A consumer's responsibility includes
questions.explanation: Responsible consumers read labels, keep receipts and report bad products.

questions.topic: Rights and Responsibilities of a Consumer
questions.stem: When a consumer insists on knowing the ingredients, weight and expiry date of a product, the right exercised is the right to
questions.explanation: Accurate facts about products are part of the right to information.

questions.stem: The best source of reliable information about a packaged food product is the
questions.explanation: Labels give ingredients, weight, manufacture and expiry dates and NAFDAC number.

questions.stem: The agency responsible for regulating food, drugs and cosmetics in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: NAFDAC regulates food, drugs, cosmetics, chemicals and packaged water.

questions.stem: The federal body that replaced the Consumer Protection Council and now enforces consumer protection and fair competition is the
options: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission
questions.explanation: The FCCPC was created by the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2018.

questions.stem: Comparing prices and quality in several shops before buying is a principle of
questions.explanation: Comparison shopping helps consumers get value for money.

questions.stem: A middleman who buys goods in large quantities and sells to retailers is a
questions.explanation: Wholesalers link producers and retailers.

questions.stem: Reusing glass jars for storing grains in the kitchen is an example of
questions.explanation: Reuse reduces waste, an aspect of the 3 Rs: reduce, reuse, recycle.

questions.stem: Buying goods without previous planning because of their attractive display is
questions.explanation: Impulse buying is unplanned and often wasteful.

questions.stem: Bulk buying is most advantageous when the family
options: lives in a one-room apartment with no shelves at all
has adequate storage and the goods are non-perishable
questions.explanation: Bulk buying saves money only when goods keep well and storage is available.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the term decision-making. [2 marks]
(b) List and explain five steps in decision-making. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Choosing the best course of action from two or more alternatives
2 marks: Identify/define the problem
2 marks: Seek possible alternatives
2 marks: Consider the consequences of each alternative
2 marks: Choose the best alternative and act on it
2 marks: Evaluate the result / accept responsibility
questions.explanation: Decision-making is choosing among alternatives. Steps: identify the problem, list alternatives, weigh consequences, choose and act, then evaluate.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following: (i) peak load period (ii) dovetailing (iii) work simplification. [6 marks]
(b) State three ways of reducing fatigue in household work. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Peak load: time of day with the heaviest workload
2 marks: Dovetailing: doing two or more tasks at the same time
2 marks: Work simplification: easier, quicker ways of doing a task with less energy
2 marks: Use labour-saving equipment and proper work heights
2 marks: Take short rest periods and alternate heavy with light tasks
2 marks: Plan work and share tasks among family members
questions.explanation: Peak load is the busiest period; dovetailing combines tasks; work simplification finds easier methods. Fatigue is reduced by equipment, rest, alternating tasks, planning and sharing work.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a nuclear family and an extended family. [4 marks]
(b) Discuss four functions of the family. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Nuclear family: father, mother and their children
2 marks: Extended family: nuclear family plus relatives such as grandparents, uncles, cousins
2 marks: Reproduction: bearing children to continue the family
2 marks: Socialisation/education of children in values and culture
2 marks: Economic support: food, shelter, clothing
2 marks: Emotional support, love, security and protection
questions.explanation: The nuclear family is parents and children; the extended family adds other relatives. Families reproduce, socialise, provide economically and give emotional security.

questions.stem:
(a) Name three types of seams. [3 marks]
(b) Describe how to make a French seam. [6 marks]
(c) State three ways of disposing of fullness in garment making. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Plain/open seam
1 mark: French seam
1 mark: Flat fell (run and fell) or overlaid seam
2 marks: Place wrong sides together and stitch 6 mm from the edge
2 marks: Trim the raw edges close to the stitching and press
2 marks: Turn right sides together, enclosing the raw edges, and stitch about 6 mm from the fold
1 mark: Darts
1 mark: Gathers
1 mark: Pleats or tucks
questions.explanation: Seams include plain, French and flat fell. A French seam is stitched wrong sides together, trimmed, then stitched right sides together to enclose edges. Fullness is controlled by darts, gathers, tucks and pleats.

questions.stem:
(a) List in order four processes in laundering a cotton garment. [4 marks]
(b) Explain how to remove each of the following stains: (i) fresh blood (ii) tea (iii) grease. [6 marks]
(c) Give two reasons for starching. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Sorting
1 mark: Steeping/soaking
1 mark: Washing
1 mark: Rinsing, then drying and ironing
2 marks: Fresh blood: soak in cold salt water, then wash in warm soapy water
2 marks: Tea: pour borax solution or hot water through the stain, then wash
2 marks: Grease: dab with a grease solvent or wash in hot soapy water with detergent
1 mark: Gives stiffness and crispness
1 mark: Keeps dirt off the fibres, making the next wash easier
questions.explanation: Laundering: sort, steep, wash, rinse, dry, iron. Blood needs cold salt water; tea responds to borax; grease to solvent or hot detergent. Starch stiffens and protects fabric.

questions.stem:
A toddler lives in a flat with a gas cooker, trailing extension cables, a wet bathroom floor and medicines on a low shelf.
(a) Identify four dangers to the child in this home. [4 marks]
(b) Suggest one way of removing each danger identified in (a). [4 marks]
(c) Describe the first aid for a minor scald on the child's arm. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Burns or scalds from the cooker
1 mark: Electric shock or tripping from trailing cables
1 mark: Falls on the wet floor
1 mark: Poisoning from medicines
1 mark: Keep child out of the kitchen; turn pan handles inwards; fit cooker guard
1 mark: Shorten or secure cables; cover unused sockets
1 mark: Dry floors promptly; use non-slip mats
1 mark: Lock medicines in a high cabinet
2 marks: Cool the area under clean cool running water for at least 10 minutes
1 mark: Remove tight items such as bangles before swelling
1 mark: Cover loosely with a clean non-fluffy dressing; do not apply oil or burst blisters; seek help if severe
questions.explanation: Dangers are burns, shocks, falls and poisoning, removed by guarding the cooker, securing cables, drying floors and locking up medicines. A minor scald is cooled under running water, jewellery removed and the area covered loosely, without oil.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a family budget? [2 marks]
(b) State five steps in preparing a family budget. [5 marks]
(c) Mr Okon earns N120,000 a month. He spends N30,000 on rent, N45,000 on food, N20,000 on transport and N10,000 on utilities, and saves the rest. Calculate his monthly savings and the percentage of income saved. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: A plan of expected income and expenditure for a period
1 mark: Determine total family income
1 mark: List family needs and wants
1 mark: Estimate the cost of each item
1 mark: Allocate money, including savings
1 mark: Compare with income, adjust and evaluate
1 mark: Total spent: 30,000 + 45,000 + 20,000 + 10,000 = N105,000
2 marks: Savings: 120,000 - 105,000 = N15,000
2 marks: Percentage saved: 15,000/120,000 x 100 = 12.5%
questions.explanation: A budget plans income against expenditure. Total spending is N105,000, leaving N15,000 saved, which is 12.5% of N120,000.

questions.stem:
(a) What is the capital market? [2 marks]
(b) Name three instruments traded on the Nigerian capital market. [3 marks]
(c) State four benefits of investing in shares to a family. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Market for buying and selling long-term securities such as shares and bonds
1 mark: Shares/stocks
1 mark: Government or corporate bonds
1 mark: Mutual funds/unit trusts or debentures
2 marks: Dividend income
2 marks: Capital appreciation as share prices rise
2 marks: Bonus shares or rights issues
2 marks: Shares can be used as collateral or sold for cash when needed
questions.explanation: The capital market deals in long-term funds through shares, bonds and mutual funds. Shares give dividends, capital gains, bonus shares and can be sold or pledged.

questions.topic: Rights and Responsibilities of a Consumer
questions.stem:
(a) State four rights of a consumer. [4 marks]
(b) State four responsibilities of a consumer. [4 marks]
(c) Name two agencies that protect consumers in Nigeria and one function of each. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Right to safety
1 mark: Right to information
1 mark: Right to choose
1 mark: Right to redress or to be heard
1 mark: Read labels and instructions
1 mark: Keep receipts and warranties
1 mark: Report substandard goods to authorities
1 mark: Use products as directed and pay fair prices
2 marks: NAFDAC: regulates food, drugs and cosmetics
2 marks: SON or FCCPC: sets product standards or handles consumer complaints
questions.explanation: Consumers have rights to safety, information, choice, redress and to be heard, and responsibilities to read labels, keep receipts and report bad products. NAFDAC, SON and FCCPC protect them.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following colour schemes: (i) monochromatic (ii) analogous (iii) complementary. [6 marks]
(b) Give three ways of improving a sitting room at low cost. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Monochromatic: tints and shades of one hue
2 marks: Analogous: colours next to one another on the colour wheel
2 marks: Complementary: colours opposite each other on the wheel
2 marks: Repaint walls or rearrange furniture
2 marks: Make cushion covers, curtains or throws from cheap fabric
2 marks: Add plants, flowers or handmade ornaments
questions.explanation: Monochromatic uses one hue; analogous uses neighbours on the wheel; complementary uses opposites. Low-cost improvements include repainting, rearranging, home-made soft furnishings and plants.
